findings.title: p.exe running in attacker staging directory under Domain Admin account
findings.description: p.exe (PID 8260) was found running from C:\Windows\Temp\Perfmon\p.exe, a non-standard staging path. The process runs under spsql (Domain Admin S-1-5-21-...-512) and has loaded network (WININET, WS2_32, DNSAPI), crypto (rsaenh, bcrypt, CRYPTSP), and authentication (Secur32, SSPICLI) DLLs consistent with a C2 implant. Post-launch DLL loading on 2018-09-05 (6 days after start) indicates the implant remained active and expanded capabilities. Extraction succeeded but mcp__hash_file/mcp__yara_scan are not available in this session; binary malware classification cannot be verified per protocol.

evidence.raw_tool_output: 8260 5948 p.exe 0x8c88af601580 2 - 0 False 2018-08-30 22:15:18.000000 UTC N/A | DLLs: WININET.dll 2018-08-30 22:15:19 UTC, rsaenh.dll, bcrypt.dll, WS2_32.dll, mpr.dll loaded 2018-09-05 12:13:26 UTC

findings.title: Active C2 beaconing to 172.16.4.10:8080 (multiple ESTABLISHED connections)
findings.description: Three simultaneous ESTABLISHED TCP connections from the victim (172.16.6.11) to 172.16.4.10:8080 were found at capture time, along with eight CLOSE_WAIT connections to the same endpoint. HTTP port 8080 with persistent ESTABLISHED sessions and beacon-like CLOSE_WAIT accumulation is consistent with a C2 implant maintaining a keep-alive channel. p.exe has WININET loaded, supporting HTTP-based C2 communication.

findings.title: WMI-based remote execution used for initial access (WmiPrvSE → powershell.exe)
findings.description: WmiPrvSE.exe (PID 2876, child of svchost PID 868) spawned powershell.exe (PID 8712) at 2018-08-30 16:43:36 UTC. WmiPrvSE ran as NT Authority/NetworkService (S-1-5-20), but the spawned powershell runs as spsql (Domain Admin), indicating the attacker used spsql credentials to authenticate a remote WMI connection that executed PowerShell on the victim host.

evidence.raw_tool_output: 2876 868 WmiPrvSE.exe 0x8c88b14e7580 | child: 8712 2876 powershell.exe 0x8c88b47b9080 11 - 0 False 2018-08-30 16:43:36 UTC | getsids PID 8712: S-1-5-21-...-512 Domain Admins

findings.title: PowerShell remoting chain (32-bit PS -s flag) used to stage and execute p.exe
findings.description: powershell.exe (PID 8712, 64-bit) spawned a 32-bit SysWOW64 powershell.exe (PID 5848) with flags '-Version 5.1 -s -NoLogo -NoProfile'. The -s flag indicates stdin-driven PS Remoting (engine mode). This 32-bit shell then spawned cmd.exe (PID 5948) at 2018-08-30 22:15:18 UTC with command 'C:\WINDOWS\system32\cmd.exe /C c:\windows\temp\perfmon\p.exe', which in turn launched p.exe. Using 32-bit PowerShell avoids certain 64-bit detection and constrained language mode controls.

evidence.raw_tool_output: 5948 5848 cmd.exe | cmd cmdline: C:\WINDOWS\system32\cmd.exe /C c:\windows\temp\perfmon\p.exe | 8260 5948 p.exe 2018-08-30 22:15:18 UTC

findings.title: Lateral movement via SMB to 172.16.7.15 and 172.16.4.5 with RDP attempts
findings.description: Two ESTABLISHED SMB (port 445) connections from the victim to internal hosts (172.16.7.15 and 172.16.4.5) were active at capture time. Seven CLOSED RDP (port 3389) connections to 172.16.4.5 indicate repeated remote desktop attempts, consistent with the attacker using Domain Admin credentials to spread laterally through the environment.

findings.title: Active Directory LDAP reconnaissance to 172.16.4.4:389
findings.description: A CLOSED TCP connection from the victim to 172.16.4.4:389 (standard LDAP) was recorded in netscan. Port 389 is the domain controller LDAP port used for AD enumeration. This connection, combined with Domain Admin context, indicates the attacker queried Active Directory for account, group, or host enumeration.

findings.title: WinRM connection to 172.16.5.21:5985 — potential PowerShell remoting lateral move
findings.description: A CLOSED TCP connection to 172.16.5.21:5985 (WS-Management / WinRM) was captured. Port 5985 is used for PowerShell Remoting (HTTP transport). A CLOSED state means the session completed before capture. Given the attacker's use of PowerShell remoting and Domain Admin privileges, this likely represents a successful lateral move to 172.16.5.21.

findings.title: p.exe spawned rundll32.exe children with no command lines (plugin/implant execution)
findings.description: p.exe (PID 8260) spawned three rundll32.exe processes (PIDs 5768, 7552, 1424) across 2018-09-05 to 2018-09-06, with all command lines blank. rundll32 with no visible arguments is a hallmark of reflective DLL loading or in-memory module execution. The wide time span (>8 days from p.exe start) confirms the implant remained active and executed modules on demand.

findings.title: PowerShell PID 5848 spawned multiple rundll32.exe — attacker staging activity
findings.description: The attacker-controlled powershell.exe (PID 5848, SysWOW64) spawned six rundll32.exe processes (PIDs 6768, 5452, 5588, 4108, 2216, 8148) between 2018-08-30 18:31 and 2018-08-31 00:56 UTC. All have blank command lines. This pattern is consistent with a PowerShell implant reflectively loading successive DLL-based modules before dropping and executing p.exe.

findings.title: No registry-based persistence detected; svcscan reveals no malicious services
findings.description: Run and RunOnce keys were enumerated across all hives; no attacker-controlled entries found under spsql or HKLM. The spsql ntuser.dat Run/RunOnce keys are empty. svcscan showed only VMware tools, standard Windows services, and the F-Response Subject forensic agent. No persistence via scheduled tasks or services was identified in memory.

evidence.raw_tool_output: spsql Run key: no data entries. spsql RunOnce key: no data entries. svcscan: F-Response Subject (subject_srv.exe) and VMware tools only — no user-writable-path services

findings.description: malfind flagged two RWX regions in OUTLOOK.EXE (PID 8128) beginning with bytes 64 74 72 52 (ASCII: dtrR). These were initially noted as suspicious injection candidates.

findings.title: Incoming SMB connection from 172.16.6.14 to this host
findings.description: netscan shows an ESTABLISHED TCP connection from 172.16.6.14:65368 to 172.16.6.11:445 (this host). An inbound SMB connection could indicate another attacker-controlled host connecting to this machine, a DC performing domain operations, or the forensic investigator host. Cannot determine directionality without additional host context.

findings.title: procdump.exe found in Dashlane application directory
findings.description: filescan identified procdump.exe at \Users\tdungan\AppData\Roaming\Dashlane\6.2.0.12026\procdump.exe. procdump is a Sysinternals process dumping tool that can be used for LSASS credential dumping. The path under Dashlane is unusual. No corresponding process entry was found, so it may have been previously executed and exited, or staged but not yet run.
